tasks.short: Monitor network traffic, security and capacity

steps.what: Draft the anomaly note from the rows

loop.input: view rows and the anomaly template
loop.output: a note that cites circuit or device ids
loop.check: Each anomaly cites a circuit id or a device id on the view
loop.stop: One draft; drop a line with no id and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: The sentence that says why a spike matters is not a threshold

steps.what: Send open anomalies to the operator

tasks.design: A {BI} view shows traffic, security events and capacity for circuit and device ids from the {OPS_SYSTEM}. A bounded note in {DOCS} drafts an anomaly list from those rows only. The telecommunications specialist decides which anomalies matter and files that note. The view does not name a person. This task does not change the network and does not file a statutory incident report.
tasks.previous_blocker: Charts were copied out of several consoles, so an anomaly note could not show which counter it used.
tasks.enabler_now: Traffic, event and capacity exports can share a circuit id and a time window.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a spike is harmless for this business is not a threshold.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist decides which anomalies are real and which can wait.

ambition.what: Review capacity every week, not only when a link is already full

tasks.altitude: Less time building the picture. The specialist can refuse an anomaly that has no row, and no change is made from this task.

reach.task: Investigate the anomaly the specialist marked
reach.learn: Which anomalies are signed as real and which were filed as noise

evidence.claim: Digest [S7] and [S8] describe a managed detection service for mid-size firms that uses models to speed investigation, while analysts still decide.

Digest [S13] reports an observational study of live security operations with shorter resolve times after a generative assistant versus matched peers. It was not a randomised trial, and it does not cover capacity charts.
Digest [S22] says security logging must stay necessary and proportionate. The view stores circuit and device counters and security event ids, not message contents.
Digest [S17] and [S19] say sector and size decide scope, and firms in scope report incidents at 24 hours, 72 hours and one month. This task does not file those reports.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so this task files a note and does not push a change.

assumptions: Focal role is the telecommunications specialist. The task is monitoring and the analysis note. Changing the network, and filing a statutory incident report, are later tasks.
Input contract: window start, window end, circuit id, device id, counter or event id, value, site. Producer is the monitoring export. A row with no circuit id and no device id is dropped.
Use the existing dashboard and alert rules before custom code. The meeting prior overstates this task: most time is on the screen. A short review remains for the note.
The view is not staff monitoring. Per-person content is out of scope. Works-council consent would be required before any such view, and this design does not build it.
unknowns: Whether this firm is in scope of the incident-reporting duty.
Which links have no counter export.
Who is on call when the specialist is absent.
research_questions: What share of alerts last month had no circuit id?
How often is the first anomaly note overturned?

already_counted.description: Watch time on the view stays with the specialist
Anomaly decision stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Keep alert thresholds and view filters aligned with new circuit types

approvals.approved_version: anomaly note signed for this window

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many links have no export, so the specialist still assembles those charts by hand. The high case assumes the view is complete but every anomaly decision stays manual. Network changes and statutory incident reports are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Manage accounts and passwords for system access

steps.what: Submit the access or password request
Classify the request into a category

loop.input: request text and the category list
loop.check: The category is grant, change, remove or password, and is on the list
loop.stop: If none fits, leave a blank and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text asks do not match a keyword table reliably

steps.what: Sign the standard profile for this period
Sign the exception or privileged request
Apply a signed profile grant or reset
Apply the signed exception on the system
Reset a privileged password by hand

tasks.design: A {WORKFLOW} request carries employee id, role code, site, system id and request type, with joiner, mover and leaver dates from {HCM}. A bounded pass on the {HELPDESK} only suggests the category. A standard profile on the {OPS_SYSTEM} applies only after the telecommunications specialist has signed that profile version. Exceptions and privileged passwords are signed one by one and applied by hand or by a job bound to that signature. A model does not choose who gets access.
tasks.previous_blocker: Access asks arrived by mail with no role code, so a job could not tell a standard profile from a privileged grant.
tasks.enabler_now: Employee id and role code can come from the staff record, and the profile map is a table the specialist can sign.
tasks.still_hard: A privileged account, or a role that does not match the map, is still a judgement. A wrong grant is costly to undo.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist signs the profile version and every exception, and refuses a request with no manager.

ambition.what: Staff at small sites can request a standard password reset without a visit

tasks.altitude: Standard grants follow the signed profile. The specialist can block any live change that is not that version or a signed exception.

reach.task: See why an access request was refused
reach.learn: Which profile version is current and which requests are still unsigned

evidence.claim: Digest [S1] and [S2] say a service desk can suggest a ticket category for a person to review. That is used here only to class the access request, not to grant it.
Digest [S15] reports a vendor self-service claim of fewer tickets, with no published baseline. That figure is not used as a saving for password resets.
Digest [S22] says security logging must stay necessary and proportionate. The access log stores request id, role code and result, not a person's messages.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so a grant or a password change is never applied unattended.

assumptions: Focal role is the telecommunications specialist. The task is access and passwords on telecommunications systems, not every application in the company.

Input contract: request id, employee id, role code, site, system id, request type, manager id, privileged flag. Producer is the people manager, or the staff system for a joiner, mover or leaver. A request with no employee id or no manager id is rejected by rule.
Use the identity store's own joiner flow and the helpdesk password action before custom code. A model does not score the person and does not choose the profile.
Standard resets are not staff monitoring. If those logs were later used to watch staff, works-council consent would be required. This design does not do that.
unknowns: Which telecommunications systems have a job interface for accounts.
Who may sign a privileged grant when the specialist is away.
Whether a shared site-phone password is in this task.
research_questions: What share of requests sits outside the standard profile?
How many privileged password resets occur in a month?

already_counted.description: Exception and privileged sign-off stays with the specialist
Hands-on privileged reset stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Update the profile map when a role code changes
Managers resubmit requests the form rejects

approvals.approved_version: standard profile version signed for this period
exception or privileged request signed for this request id
the same signed standard profile version
the same signed exception for this request id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many systems have no account interface and most requests are exceptions, so the specialist still grants them by hand. The high case assumes standard profiles apply after one signed version, while every privileged grant and every failed match still takes specialist time. Other application accounts are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The specialist reads a prepared traffic and capacity view instead of assembling it, and still signs every access change outside the standard profile.
reach: Network operators investigate the anomalies the specialist has marked, and leave the rest.
People managers see which access request was signed and which was refused.
skills_to_grow: Separate a counter that is a query from an anomaly that needs a signature.
Bind an access change to a role code and a request id.
Keep a privileged password reset on a manual queue.
role.ambitious_version: Each week has a signed anomaly note, and every access change is either the signed standard profile or a signed exception.
